messages.author: f57c96af63c64056
messages.subject: Constraining variances to be equal
parts:
Hi,

I have a two item construct that i wish to implement CFA on.
I know that most research literature says at minimum you should have 3 items per construct.
Two papers i have found specify that two item factors are OK if correlations among the items in the factor must be extremely high (r > 0.7) while remaining uncorrelated with the items that are not associated with the factor [1].
Another paper also suggests that a two item factor is possible if the errors on the items do not co-vary and the loadings are restricted to be equal [2],
Now i know its not ideal but i would like to learn how to do the following in Lavaan

1)  How do i restrict the loadings to be equal in lavaan for a two item construct when specifying the formula?

Thank you all for your generous help

[1] - A Beginner’s Guide to Factor Analysis: Focusing on Exploratory Factor Analysis - Yong, A.G. and Pearce, S
[2] - Latent Variable Modeling Using R pg 40

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Constraining variances to be equal
parts:
You can make the model identified by constraining residual variances to equality. Just give them the same label. If F is your factor and indicators are Y1 and Y2:

F =~ Y1 + Y2
Y1~~a*Y1
Y2~~a*Y2

That's it.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Constraining variances to be equal
parts: Estimation is simultaneous. The program is not solving these equations. It is solving a matrix equation for the model-implied moments as a function of model parameters. So instead of 2 parameters, there is  only 1. If you ever find that order makes a difference, then something is wrong.
